A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PipeFusion. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching material moved into v4's appendices.

before.justification: V3 reports original latency, scalability, memory, image-quality, and ablation results for Pixart, SD3-medium, and Flux.1-dev.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds an A100/NVLink evaluation in Appendix B, Table 4.

M1.justification: Patch and layer partitioning, pipelined execution, stale-KV reuse, asynchronous communication, and synchronous warmup remain unchanged. V4's patch-count recommendation restates the existing ablation finding; hybrid deployment and video extensions are discussed without introducing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: V4 Appendix B extends evaluation to a high-bandwidth deployment scenario using A100 GPUs connected through NVLink, beyond v3's L40/PCIe environment. The image-generation tasks and COCO coverage remain unchanged; video and few-step models are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their original comparators, including tensor parallelism, DistriFusion, SP-Ring, SP-Ulysses, USP, and the original implementation where applicable. The added NVLink table evaluates existing comparison methods; newly cited video and distilled models are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V4 adds an eight-A100/NVLink evaluation at 1024px, 2048px, and 4096px and introduces the CommShare metric in Equation 2. Existing L40 settings, schedulers, warmup defaults, patch-count searches, and the 30,000-image COCO evaluation protocol are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds hardware-interconnect sensitivity testing, a communication-overhead estimate derived from existing 4096px timings, and a parking-meter visual example. The original patch-count and warmup ablations are retained in Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report latency averaged over five runs without seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4's checklist acknowledges the absence of uncertainty estimates but does not establish a changed repetition or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Original latency plots, memory results, FID scores, and warmup results are retained. V4 adds NVLink results, derived communication shares of 4.6% versus 17.9%, and another visual example. In the new Table 4, PipeFusion takes 2.59 seconds at 2048px, slower than SP-Ring's 2.46 and DistriFusion's 2.48, contradicting the accompanying claim that it is always fastest.

T1.justification: V4 introduces Equation 2, defining CommShare by subtracting one-eighth of single-GPU latency from eight-GPU latency and normalizing the residual. This adds a mathematical definition and associated calculation. The diffusion update, pipeline-utilization formula, and communication/memory cost analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that temporal redundancy enables patch-level pipelining with reduced communication and memory costs, competitive image quality, and superior L40 inference performance. The rewritten introduction and conclusion largely restate these claims and summarize already reported findings.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands applicability and limitations through Section 5: dependence on multiple diffusion steps, hybrid deployment across different interconnects, and arguments for extending PipeFusion to video. It also reframes high-resolution scalability using estimated communication overhead and adds an interpretation of NVLink robustness. V3 discussed warmup costs and future multinode scaling but lacked these specific boundaries and extension arguments.

D1.justification: V4 identifies the A100/NVLink hardware used for the added experiment and newly attributes the showcase prompts to DistriFusion, distinguishing them from FID evaluation. Existing software versions, L40 specifications, COCO preparation details, and the source-code URL are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds an explicit comparison with GPipe and citations supporting discussion of few-step models and video generation, including Flux.1-schnell, distribution-matching distillation, Mean Flows, Wan, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideo. LightSeq and Mooncake references are removed. These are bounded extensions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V4 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction and background, merges the tensor/sequence-parallelism subsections, incorporates quality results into Experiments, and moves visual examples and ablations into appendices. It also adds a limitations section and conference checklist and updates author and publication information.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout throughout. V3 Figures 9 and 10 become v4 Figure 9's panels; the combined quality display is split into main-text Table 2 and appendix Figure 10, with an additional image row. Ablation displays move to Appendix B, and Table 4 is added; the original performance plots themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The added hardware-sensitivity evidence and explicit few-step limitation modestly improve the paper's evidential breadth and applicability guidance while preserving its original method and results. The gain is limited by an inaccurate interpretation: Table 4 shows PipeFusion losing to SP-Ring and DistriFusion at 2048px despite claiming the lowest latency at every resolution. The reported values nevertheless expose this exception and make the broader performance boundary assessable.
